sentences.text:
THIS MFA, COMING ON FOR ADMISSION, THIS DAY,
JUDGMENT WAS DELIVERED THEREIN AS UNDER:
CORAM: HON'BLE MR JUSTICE N S SANJAY GOWDA  ORAL JUDGMENT 1.
Being dissatisfied with the award of compensation of Rs.2,43,979/-, the claimant is in this appeal challenging the reduction of his compensation to the extent of 50% and also seeking for enhancement.
2. The claimant was a pillion rider in a motorcycle in Bajaj M 80 two-wheeher when it was hit by a Hero Honda Splendor motorcycle which has resulted in grievous injuries to him.
3. The Tribunal on considering the medical evidence adduced has come to the conclusion that the claimant has suffered whole body disability at 10%.
In my view, this assessment of disability at 10% cannot be found fault with.
4. The Tribunal has, however, gone on to hold that the rider of the Bajaj M80 in which the claimant was traveling was also responsible to the extent of 50%.
It is to be stated here that the claimant has preferred a claim petition only against the owner of a motorcycle alleging that the driver of the motorcycle was responsible for the accident.
It is settled law that it is open for the claimant to choose a tortfeasor of his choice and therefore, the Tribunal could not have reduced the compensation to the extent of 50%.
Consequently, this finding is set aside.
5. As far as compensation is concerned, as already stated above, the assessment of disability cannot be found fault with.

As the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority has determined the notional income as Rs.8,500/- for the accident of the year 2014, it would be appropriate to determine the notional income of the claimant at Rs.8,500/-.
7. Consequently, the claimant would be entitled to a sum of Rs.1,32,600/- (Rs.8,500/- X 12 X '13' X 10%) towards 'loss of future earnings'.
8. The Tribunal has awarded Rs.16,979/- towards 'medical bills' and Rs.20,000/- towards 'food and nourishment charges'.
The said sums are just and proper and are accordingly affirmed 9.
The Tribunal has awarded Rs.30,000/- towards 'pain and sufferings' and Rs.30,000/- towards 'loss of amenities'.
In my view, it would be appropriate to enhance the same to Rs.50,000/- each.
10. The Tribunal has taken the laid-up period as six months.

Since the income is taken as Rs.8,500/-, NC: 2024:KHC:50925 the claimant would be entitled to a sum of Rs.51,000/-
(Rs.8,500/- X 6 months) towards loss of earnings during laid up period.

11. Consequently, the award of the Tribunal is modified and the following sums are awarded as compensation:
